card: This PR backports PR #35168 to the 31.x release branch to fix a validation assertion crash (#35050). In v31.1, LoadBlockIndex adds pruned blocks on stale forks to m_blocks_unlinked if their parent is header-only, which violates internal invariants and crashes nodes configured with -checkblockindex (such as regtest functional test runs). The fix requires BLOCK_HAVE_DATA before adding blocks to m_blocks_unlinked and backports the regression test.
evidence: Commit 6cedc5d47e: "LoadBlockIndex() adds to m_blocks_unlinked based only on nTx > 0, without checking BLOCK_HAVE_DATA... Check that BLOCK_HAVE_DATA is set before inserting into m_blocks_unlinked. Fixes #35050."
Description notes that "The added feature_prune_stale_fork.py fails against the v31.1 release binary on the assertion above and passes on this branch"
problem: In v31.1, LoadBlockIndex inserts blocks into m_blocks_unlinked based on nTx > 0 without checking whether the block data was pruned. For a pruned block whose parent is header-only, this violates the invariant that m_blocks_unlinked entries must have data on disk, causing nodes running with -checkblockindex (such as regtest functional tests) to crash on an assertion failure during startup or when connecting blocks.

risk.why: A flaw in block index reconstruction during startup could corrupt the unlinked block tracking graph and cause nodes to fail to connect valid chain tips.

scope_notes: Clean backport of 2 commits from master (#35168) touching validation.cpp, test_runner.py, and adding feature_prune_stale_fork.py.
summary: Backports PR #35168 to the 31.x release branch. It ensures that LoadBlockIndex only adds blocks to m_blocks_unlinked during startup if the block data is actually available on disk (BLOCK_HAVE_DATA), and adds a functional test covering the invariant.
